name: Scapebird
overview: The scapebird ritual described in Leviticus 14 illustrates a divinely ordained process of cleansing from leprosy, where two live birds are used symbolically in the purification ceremony. One bird is killed over running water, and the living bird is dipped in its blood along with cedar wood, scarlet, and hyssop, then sprinkled upon the person to be cleansed, signifying the removal of impurity. The living bird is then released into the open field, representing the removal of sin and the restoration of the individual to the community. This act of atonement extends even to the cleansing of a house, emphasizing God's provision for holiness and restoration through prescribed means.
